data.title: Samsung forecast to overtake Apple in global smartphone shipments in 2026: report
data.summary: A new industry report forecasts that Samsung Electronics Co. will reclaim its position as the top global smartphone vendor in 2026, surpassing Apple Inc. Samsung's broad product portfolio and strong distribution networks are cited as key factors, while Apple faces potential price hikes and limited impact from its upcoming foldable iPhone. Samsung's smartphone shipments are expected to increase by 0.8%, while Apple's are projected to decline by 2.1%.

data.title: Jim Cramer Defends Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) Amid Memory Shortage Pressure And Mixed Earnings Results
data.summary: Jim Cramer has defended Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) despite facing pressure from a global memory chip shortage and mixed earnings results. Cramer highlighted Apple's efforts in American manufacturing and the challenges in memory procurement due to high demand from other tech giants. While iPhone revenue showed significant growth, the Services, iPad, and wearables segments underperformed, raising concerns about Apple's reliance on iPhone performance for overall growth.

data.title: Ireland gains 17.1bn dollars in Apple tax after state aid escrow release
data.summary: Ireland has received $17.1 billion in tax from Apple, representing 66.7% of the company's worldwide cash tax payments, following the release of escrowed funds related to a European Commission state aid decision. This disclosure comes from Apple's public country-by-country report for fiscal 2025, filed under EU transparency law, which also reveals that Irish entities booked 43.6% of Apple's total revenue and 36% of its pre-tax profit. The report provides an early template for similar disclosures expected from other major multinationals under new EU regulations.

data.title: Apple cutting hundreds more jobs in shift toward AI
data.summary: Apple is eliminating over 200 jobs as it refocuses on artificial intelligence, particularly by revamping its Siri digital assistant. The job cuts affect approximately 100 positions within the Vision Pro team and another 100 in Siri and Intelligent Systems Experience groups, as Apple shifts from legacy engineering roles to specialists in generative AI. This move aims to improve Siri's capabilities, which have lagged behind competitors, and reallocate resources from the commercially disappointing Vision Pro headset.

data.title: Nvidia customers notified about AI-related price hikes above 15%
data.summary: Nvidia's biggest customers have been informed of price increases exceeding 15% for servers containing its AI chips, effective early next year. These hikes are driven by soaring memory chip costs from manufacturers like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, which are struggling to meet the surging demand for AI infrastructure. This move highlights the leverage memory chip makers have and could complicate large tech companies' AI data center build-out plans.

data.title: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) Cuts Over 200 Jobs In Siri And Vision Pro As Company Pivots To AI And Smart Glasses
data.summary: Apple is cutting over 200 jobs in its Siri and Vision Pro divisions as it reallocates resources towards artificial intelligence and next-generation hardware like smart glasses. The restructuring impacts roughly 100 Vision Pro roles and 100 Siri/Intelligent Systems Experience positions, driven by a shift to an AI-enhanced Siri and a tactical retreat from certain Vision Pro content development due to high costs and slow adoption. Despite these adjustments, Apple affirms its commitment to the Vision Pro hardware and visionOS, with a potential updated model by late 2028, and its stock shows investor confidence in the company's broader strategic direction.

data.title: Apple faces class action over alleged ‘bricking’ of older Apple Watch models
data.summary: Apple is facing a new class action lawsuit alleging that the company prematurely ended software support for several older Apple Watch models, effectively "bricking" them and forcing consumers to buy new devices. The lawsuit claims Apple's watchOS 27 update is incompatible with models like the SE 2, Series 6, 7, 8, and Ultra 1, which were sold recently and had not yet reached their useful life. The plaintiff, Richard Goetz, alleges unfair business practices and seeks to represent California consumers who purchased these affected Apple Watch models.

data.title: Compatible Verizon phones can send satellite texts as another Hawaii storm nears
data.summary: Verizon is preparing its network in Hawaii for an approaching tropical storm, following Hurricane Lala, by reinforcing infrastructure, refueling generators, and staging mobile equipment. The company is offering customer relief through August 31st, including waived charges and unlimited usage for eligible customers. Verizon also highlights the use of satellite messaging on compatible devices like the iPhone 14/18+ and Google Pixel 9+ for critical communications if terrestrial services fail, urging customers to familiarize themselves with these features.

data.title: Apple Reportedly Shifts Focus To AI And Smart Glasses With Job Cuts In Siri And Vision Pro Teams
data.summary: Apple has reportedly cut over 200 jobs across its Siri, software engineering, and Vision Pro divisions as it shifts focus towards artificial intelligence and future smart glasses hardware. The company is re-architecting Siri for AI enhancement and scaling back internal Vision Pro gaming and immersive video content production due to cost and adoption challenges. While the Vision Pro hardware line remains active, near-term hardware priorities are pivoting towards developing simpler smart glasses, with a potential updated Vision Pro model considered for late 2028.

data.title: Apple Cuts Jobs in Siri, Vision Pro Immersive Video and Gaming Teams
data.summary: Apple Inc. is implementing job cuts across its Siri digital assistant and Vision Pro headset teams, as well as its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which handles AI features. This move is part of a broader strategy to refocus the company's efforts on developing new devices and advancing artificial intelligence capabilities.

data.title: Intel Sold $20 Billion of Stock at $95 a Share. It Now Trades Below $93.
data.summary: Intel recently raised $23 billion through a stock offering, selling approximately 242 million shares at $95 each to fund AI-driven growth opportunities. However, just eleven days later, the stock is trading below $93, leaving new buyers underwater. While this dip coincides with a broader downturn in chip stocks, the market's reluctance to maintain the $95 price suggests it's waiting for more concrete proof of Intel's projected AI demand and productive use of the raised capital.

data.title: Arista Networks Inc Stock (ANET) Moved Up by 3.08% on Aug 21: Facts Behind the Movement
data.summary: Arista Networks Inc. (ANET) saw its stock rise by 3.08% on August 21st, driven by strong quarterly financial results, an increased full-year outlook, and growing demand for AI networking fabrics. The company's expanded multi-year purchase obligations for components also reinforced investor confidence, despite some insider sales and valuation concerns. Analysts have raised price targets for ANET due to its market share gains in AI networking.

data.title: Apple Users Beware: ChatGPT’s Newest Mac Feature Could Pose a Major Privacy Risk
data.summary: OpenAI's new ChatGPT feature for Mac allows it to control Apple's Messages app, offering convenience for personal use by searching, drafting, and sending replies. However, this integration requires granting ChatGPT deep access to contacts and disk storage, raising significant privacy and security concerns, especially for business users who might unwittingly expose sensitive company data. The article highlights a potential conflict with Apple's privacy-centric reputation, as users give a powerful AI chatbot free rein over their communications and data.

data.title: Walmart will let customers use Apple Pay after holding out for more than a decade. Why it finally caved
data.summary: Walmart, after resisting for over a decade, has finally announced support for Apple Pay and other tap-to-pay methods. The retail giant previously avoided these mobile payment options to protect customer data for their own profiling and tried to launch a competing service, CurrentC, which ultimately failed. Walmart eventually developed its own platform, Walmart Pay, before finally adopting broader mobile payment support.

data.title: Walmart makes major change to how you can pay in stores
data.summary: Walmart is implementing a major change to its payment systems, introducing tap-to-pay technology at all U.S. Walmart and Sam's Club stores by the end of 2026, with expansion to fuel stations by mid-2027. This update will support options like Apple Pay and Google Pay, as well as digital versions of Walmart, Sam's Club, and OnePay cards. This move aims to provide customers with more choice and convenience, making Walmart one of the last major retailers to adopt this widely used payment method.

data.title: Walmart to accept Apple Pay and Google Pay at all U.S. stores
data.summary: Walmart announced it will begin accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay, along with other contactless payments, at all of its U.S. stores and Sam's Club locations by the end of 2026, with fuel stations following by mid-2027. This decision marks a significant reversal for the retailer, which previously favored its own payment systems. The move aims to expand customer choice and streamline the checkout process, making Walmart's payment options align more closely with other major retailers.

data.title: Walmart adding Apple Pay, other tap-to-pay options
data.summary: Walmart announced it will begin rolling out tap-to-pay options, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, in some of its U.S. stores and Sam's Club locations. This move addresses a long-standing customer request, as the retail giant previously relied on its proprietary Walmart Pay system. The company aims to implement the technology in all stores and clubs by year-end and at all fuel stations by mid-2027.

data.title: Apple Lays Off Staff As Vision Pro Demand Disappoints
data.summary: Apple Inc. has reportedly laid off at least 60 employees involved with its Vision Pro and other virtual reality projects, indicating a deceleration of its mixed-reality ambitions. This move follows reports of Apple scaling back future Vision Pro plans due to weak consumer interest, including the cancellation of a second-generation device and a cheaper "Vision Air" model. The company is now re-focusing on smart glasses and artificial intelligence, although Vision Pro development is not entirely abandoned.

data.title: Moody’s changes ARKO outlook to stable on debt reduction
data.summary: Moody's has revised ARKO Corp.'s outlook from negative to stable, while affirming its B2 corporate family rating and other related ratings. This upgrade is attributed to ARKO's improved credit metrics, which resulted from significant debt reduction and increased earnings in the first half of 2026, including proceeds from a partial IPO of ARKO Petroleum Corp. The company's adjusted debt to EBITDA ratio and EBITA coverage of interest have both improved, and Moody's anticipates ARKO will maintain strong liquidity despite a challenging consumer environment.
